chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in

A man divorced his wife three times, so she became independent from him, and he wanted to remarry her. He said to her, 'I intend to remarry you, so marry another husband.' She said to him, 'I have married another husband and my self has become lawful to you.' Will his word be accepted and will he remarry her, and what should he do? He said, 'If the woman is trustworthy, her word is accepted.' The second view in the narrations we have presented is that they should be understood as being based on a form of taqiyyah (dissimulation), because it is the school of Umar, so it is permissible that the situation necessitated him giving a ruling in it that matches his school, which indicates that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who divorces his wife three times and wants to remarry her after she marries another man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar addresses the 'takhliṣ' (purification) procedure in triple divorce, specifically examining the evidentiary weight of the woman's testimony regarding her subsequent marriage. The Imam accepts her word if she is trustworthy, while the commentary notes a secondary scholarly perspective linking this leniency to 'taqiyyah' (dissimulation) to align with the Caliph Umar's juristic school, highlighting the interplay between Imami authority and early Sunni legal traditions.
